areas.title: Getting started, harness discovery, and settings

scenarios.name: Fresh launch explains the desk and inventories recognized harnesses
steps: Launch with a fresh isolated user-data directory and capture the first screen before clicking anything.
Verify a Getting Started path explains project versus folder, chat creation, model choice, permission behavior, and where vendor processes run.
Verify every recognized installed stock harness is listed with detected, authenticated, unavailable, or needs-action state and a plain-language reason.
Verify custom direct-API choices are introduced without implying that Workhorse owns an account or subscription.
Dismiss or finish onboarding, restart, and verify its completion state is intentional and reversible from Settings.

scenarios.name: Connect stock harnesses and add both custom API shapes
steps: Open Settings to the connected-LLM surface from both onboarding and /settings.
Inspect detected Grok, Codex, and Claude rows without changing their vendor-owned login state.
Create one OpenAI Chat Completions bot and one Anthropic Messages bot using local fixture endpoints or approved endpoints.
Probe models where supported, save, disable, re-enable, edit, and remove one bot.
Verify secrets are masked and never copied into ordinary persisted state or support exports.

scenarios.name: Every settings section is reachable and persistent
steps: Walk Profile, LLMs, Skills, Usage, and Watch from the Settings header.
Change profile, appearance, and one safe preference; leave and return.
Restart Workhorse and confirm the values persist without altering vendor credentials.
Verify Back returns to the prior product context and Usage remains inside Settings.

rubric.criterion: A first-run Getting Started experience exists and explains the Workhorse mental model before the user must guess how projects, chats, folders, agents, and permissions relate.
rubric.passCriteria: Fresh launch exposes a clear onboarding path with the five named concepts, can be completed or dismissed, and can be reopened later.
rubric.evidence: First-launch screenshots, action transcript, and post-restart screenshot.

baseline.basis: Static source walk: Welcome.tsx currently offers Create a project, Link an existing folder, and Connect an agent/Start a chat but no Getting Started flow.

rubric.criterion: The first-run and LLM settings surfaces enumerate all recognized stock harnesses and custom connection shapes with honest readiness states and actionable reasons.
rubric.passCriteria: Grok, Codex, Claude, OpenAI-compatible, and Anthropic-compatible paths are visible; detected does not mean authenticated; missing binaries and login needs are explicit.
rubric.evidence: Harness inventory screenshots plus detection payloads with secrets removed.

baseline.basis: Static source walk: Settings has stock/custom rows and detection logic, while Welcome does not show the recognized inventory.

rubric.criterion: Adding, probing, editing, disabling, and deleting a custom bot round-trips without confusing provider presets with verified runtime facts.
rubric.passCriteria: Both API shapes persist their explicit URL/model/schema, probe errors are clear, and deletion does not silently retarget existing chats.
rubric.evidence: Before/after screenshots, probe transcript, saved public bot card, and affected-chat state.

rubric.criterion: Credentials remain vendor-owned or OS-encrypted and never appear in ordinary state, logs, screenshots, diagnostics, or eval artifacts.
rubric.passCriteria: A known canary secret is absent from every collected artifact and normal state backup; custom keys are recovered only through the credential boundary.
rubric.evidence: Redacted state inspection, support report, artifact scan, and credential-store test output.

rubric.criterion: Profile, LLMs, Skills, Usage, and Watch are all reachable inside Settings and retain their intended navigation hierarchy.
rubric.passCriteria: All five sections open, Usage is not promoted to a top-level sidebar product, and Back returns predictably.
rubric.evidence: Settings-tab screenshots and navigation transcript.

rubric.criterion: Safe local preferences persist across restart while vendor credentials, subscriptions, contexts, and sandboxes remain separate.
rubric.passCriteria: Profile/appearance persist, but changing one provider never changes another provider's login, plan, context, or security configuration.
rubric.evidence: Pre/post restart state, screenshots, and provider detection comparison.

scenarios.name: Create a named project, then attach folders and references
steps: Create a project by name only and verify no folder is required.
Attach two fixture folders plus file, URL, and note references.
Start chats from project home and from the global New chat path.
Verify execution cwd is explicit and additional references reach the prompt context without becoming extra projects.

scenarios.name: Exercise chat rename, title lock, archive, move, fork, and delete
steps: Create two projects and multiple chats with distinctive message text.
Manually rename a chat, continue using it, and verify the title stays locked.
Archive/unarchive, drag or place the chat into the other project, fork it, and delete only the disposable fork.
Restart and verify ownership and archived state remain correct.

scenarios.name: Search and review project state
steps: Search by project name, chat title, and distinctive transcript text.
Open the matched message and return to the project.
Review Git edits and open the chat-scoped terminal in the local fixture workspace.
Confirm archived chats and attention items remain scoped to their projects.

rubric.criterion: A project is a named container that can exist without a folder, and chats belong to exactly one project.
rubric.passCriteria: Name-only creation succeeds, project home is usable, and each created chat has one visible owner project.
rubric.evidence: Creation screenshots and persisted project/session records.

rubric.criterion: Multiple folders and non-folder references can be added later and are represented honestly in execution context.
rubric.passCriteria: Primary cwd is explicit, additional folders/references are discoverable, and no provider is told it has filesystem access that the shell did not grant.
rubric.evidence: Project UI, generated preface, and provider-side cwd/tool evidence.

rubric.criterion: A new chat is created before model selection pressure, then uses the last valid attached model without inventing a connection.
rubric.passCriteria: New chat never blocks on a brain picker; unattached providers are not silently selected; the composer remains the model-selection surface.
rubric.evidence: New-chat transcript and composer/model-menu screenshots.

rubric.criterion: Manual chat rename locks the title against later prompt-, runtime-, or provider-generated retitling.
rubric.passCriteria: After /rename or inline rename, at least three later turns and a restart leave the exact manual title unchanged.
rubric.evidence: Title timeline with timestamps, provider title events if any, and final sidebar screenshot.

rubric.criterion: Archive, unarchive, move, fork, and delete affect only the intended chat and preserve project ownership rules.
rubric.passCriteria: Each action persists after restart; deleting a fork does not delete its parent; archived chats remain attached to their project.
rubric.evidence: Before/after session records, sidebar screenshots, and restart check.

rubric.criterion: Global search, Git review, and terminal entry points lead to the exact matching chat and its scoped workspace.
rubric.passCriteria: Search finds title and transcript matches across projects; review/terminal resolve to the selected chat's local folder or managed worktree.
rubric.evidence: Search results, selected chat identity, review root, and terminal cwd.

areas.title: Provider, model, effort, and runtime identity

scenarios.name: Trace selected identity through every stock adapter
steps: For each enabled stock profile, select a non-default model and supported effort.
Send a deterministic identity probe.
Capture selected UI state, resolved launch spec, runtime/session metadata, assistant message stamp, and usage event.
Compare every layer and record any fallback or missing evidence.

scenarios.name: Switch models and providers mid-chat without stale identity
steps: Establish a distinctive first-provider fact and collect one response.
Switch model within the same provider, then switch to a different provider.
Verify vendor session ids, permissions, message stamps, context handoff, usage buckets, and visible labels.
Switch back and verify no hidden subscription, sandbox, or vendor session was merged.

scenarios.name: Trace direct-API model identity and reject silent fallback
steps: Use a local fixture endpoint that records headers/body and can return a deliberately different response model.
Send one request with each API shape and inspect the exact model, effort/thinking, history, tools, and auth fields.
Return a mismatched model id, then an unsupported-model error.
Verify Workhorse surfaces the mismatch/error rather than labeling the reply as the requested model.

rubric.criterion: Provider availability and model lists derive from detection/runtime data when available and label catalog fallbacks as unverified choices.
rubric.passCriteria: A cache/catalog row is never presented as proof of installed availability or successful authentication.
rubric.evidence: Detection payload, cache/catalog source, model menu, and connection state.

rubric.criterion: The selected provider/model is the provider/model actually launched or sent in the outbound API request.
rubric.passCriteria: Exact identifiers match between session state and launch/request evidence for every enabled profile.
rubric.evidence: Sanitized session state, launch arguments or HTTP body, and profile id.

rubric.criterion: Effort/reasoning choices are limited to values supported by the chosen model and translated exactly for the provider.
rubric.passCriteria: Unsupported levels are not offered or silently coerced; adaptive/off/max/ultra distinctions remain provider-specific.
rubric.evidence: Model menu choices and launch/request reasoning fields.

rubric.criterion: Runtime observation, transcript stamps, and usage attribution agree with the launched provider/model or expose uncertainty explicitly.
rubric.passCriteria: Selection, launch/request, runtime, transcript, and usage form one consistent provenance chain; missing runtime identity is labeled unknown, not guessed.
rubric.evidence: Five-layer provenance record defined in provider-matrix.json.

rubric.criterion: Switching provider clears stale vendor session and permission state while preserving only the portable conversation Workhorse intentionally hands over.
rubric.passCriteria: Old vendor ids/grants are absent after cross-provider switch; new messages and usage carry the new identity; portable history is explicit.
rubric.evidence: Before/after session state, provider request, transcript stamps, and usage rows.

rubric.criterion: No silent model fallback or later retitling misrepresents which brain performed a turn.
rubric.passCriteria: Fallback is either refused or visibly recorded with actual identity; manual titles stay locked; every assistant turn retains its brain stamp.
rubric.evidence: Fallback probe, message records, title timeline, and final sidebar/composer labels.

scenarios.name: Inventory the command palette and aliases for every provider
steps: Open the slash palette in one chat per profile and capture the common command set.
Exercise every documented alias through typed input, not only palette clicks.
Verify provider-native commands appear only where supported and duplicate names resolve to the intended owner.
Confirm unavailable capabilities are hidden or clearly labeled rather than accepted and ignored.

scenarios.name: Run the complete /goal lifecycle across providers
steps: Use /goal with the same deterministic objective in each profile.
Check /goal status, pause, resume, and clear.
Verify control commands do not pollute the normal transcript and the goal bar reflects state.
Restart during an active goal and verify recovery; confirm each provider receives equivalent objective semantics.

scenarios.name: Compare canonical schedule, compact, plan, and native loop behavior
steps: Create a recurring /schedule in every profile without waiting for its due time.
Inspect /plan translation and verify tool restrictions before approval.
Create enough fixture context to invoke /compact and identify native versus Workhorse checkpoint behavior.
Where a harness exposes /loop, compare it with /schedule and verify the UI explains which state Workhorse can recover.

rubric.criterion: The command palette exposes the complete Workhorse-owned command language consistently across all providers.
rubric.passCriteria: Every command in command-contract.json is reachable with the declared aliases and has an observable effect or explicit input requirement.
rubric.evidence: Per-profile command inventory and alias action transcript.

rubric.criterion: Canonical model, effort, permission, plan, and sandbox language translates to provider controls without implying identical native capabilities.
rubric.passCriteria: Each command either maps to the correct provider control, is supplied by Workhorse, or is marked unavailable; no no-op success is allowed.
rubric.evidence: Command action, capability registry row, and launch/request/security effect.

rubric.criterion: /goal set, status, pause, resume, and clear have equivalent Workhorse semantics across every provider and survive restart.
rubric.passCriteria: The same objective and lifecycle state are visible regardless of attached provider; control commands remain quiet; active state recovers.
rubric.evidence: Goal state timeline, transcript diff, restart state, and provider prompts.

rubric.criterion: /compact uses a native operation only when available and otherwise creates a portable, inspectable Workhorse checkpoint.
rubric.passCriteria: Native versus Workhorse ownership is visible; keep-note is preserved; no provider is credited with a native compact it did not execute.
rubric.evidence: Capability label, compact event/checkpoint, and restored-context probe.

rubric.criterion: /plan establishes an auditable read/research-first boundary and translates to each provider without granting write tools prematurely.
rubric.passCriteria: A write attempt in plan mode is blocked or requires an explicit mode transition; the UI does not claim a vendor-native plan when Workhorse is enforcing it.
rubric.evidence: Mode UI, provider launch/request, write-attempt result, and permission record.

rubric.criterion: Recurring intent works through the canonical /schedule language everywhere, while provider-native loop/workflow features are surfaced as optional augmentations with clear ownership.
rubric.passCriteria: Every profile can create a persisted Workhorse schedule; native /loop appears only when discovered; the user can tell which mechanism survives a Workhorse restart.
rubric.evidence: Schedule records, provider-native command inventory, and ownership labels.

areas.title: Permissions, sandboxing, tools, and trust boundaries

scenarios.name: Translate the unified permission inbox
steps: Request a fixture file read, a fixture file write, and a harmless command in Ask mode.
Choose Deny, Allow once, and Allow for session on separate requests.
Verify the decision reaches the correct provider/tool call and is not reused outside its scope.
Switch providers and verify old grants do not cross the boundary.

scenarios.name: Probe filesystem, network, and outside-workspace boundaries
steps: Repeat safe read/write probes under off, workspace, read-only, and strict where supported.
Attempt a fixture-only network request with network blocked, ask, and allowed.
Attempt to read a canary path outside the fixture workspace without exposing its contents.
Verify Workhorse blocks at its boundary before a weaker vendor permission can override it.

scenarios.name: Exercise MCP, desk tools, subagents, and cancellation
steps: Attach a deterministic local MCP fixture and invoke one read-only and one approval-requiring tool.
Spawn a bounded subagent where the profile claims support and inspect parent/child records.
Cancel the parent and verify cascading cancellation or an explicit unsupported result.
Confirm tool labels and results never pretend a provider executed a Workhorse desk action.

rubric.criterion: One permission inbox provides Deny, Allow once, and Allow for session and translates each decision to the active provider/tool call.
rubric.passCriteria: Decisions are scoped to the exact request/session, denials stop execution, and provider switches clear stale grants.
rubric.evidence: Permission UI, normalized request, provider response, and filesystem/command outcome.

rubric.criterion: Filesystem sandbox, network policy, and outside-workspace access are distinct controls with provider-honest enforcement labels.
rubric.passCriteria: Each boundary can be varied independently; Workhorse versus native enforcement is visible; blocked actions leave no side effect.
rubric.evidence: Policy state, capability label, provider launch/request, and canary outcomes.

rubric.criterion: The stricter Workhorse boundary wins over provider approval or always-approve state.
rubric.passCriteria: Network/outside-root blocks remain blocks in always-approve; no prompt or provider flag can escalate beyond the Workhorse policy.
rubric.evidence: Security decision trace and absence of network/file side effect.

rubric.criterion: Plan/read-only operation does not permit mutation until an explicit, reviewable transition.
rubric.passCriteria: A fixture write cannot complete in plan/read-only state; the transition and resulting authority are visible.
rubric.evidence: Mode/sandbox state, write attempt, permission trace, and fixture checksum.

rubric.criterion: MCP and desk tools share normalized approvals/results without leaking server credentials or bypassing profile boundaries.
rubric.passCriteria: The same fixture tool produces equivalent visible results; secrets remain redacted; approval-required calls stop on deny.
rubric.evidence: MCP request/result, permission event, tool row, and artifact secret scan.

rubric.criterion: Subagent lifecycle, resource ceilings, worktree/shared-workspace isolation, and cancellation are explicit and auditable.
rubric.passCriteria: Parent/child identity, runtime/token ceilings, isolation mode, changed files, and final/cancel state are visible or honestly unsupported.
rubric.evidence: Subagent records, worktree path, resource counters, changed-file review, and cancellation outcome.

areas.title: Conversation continuity, switching, compaction, and recovery

scenarios.name: Resume the same chat after window and process restarts
steps: Create a provider-specific fact, tool result, and unresolved next step.
Close and reopen the window, then terminate and restart the app process.
Resume the same visible chat and ask for the fact/next step.
Verify native session load when claimed and portable replay otherwise, with no duplicate turns.

scenarios.name: Switch providers using canonical portable history
steps: Establish decisions across several complete turns and include tool/thought rows.
Switch to each other profile in sequence.
Inspect serialized portable history, provider prompt, and visible transcript.
Verify complete user/assistant turns transfer, tool internals do not impersonate conversation, and truncation is disclosed.

scenarios.name: Fork, rewind, queue, cancel, and compact without corrupting lineage
steps: Fork from a known turn and make divergent decisions in parent and child.
Queue a follow-up while a long fixture turn is running, then cancel.
Rewind where available or use Workhorse lineage where not.
Compact and verify both branches retain correct ancestry and no canceled response is later appended.

rubric.criterion: Visible chat persistence and vendor-session continuity agree after window and app-process restart.
rubric.passCriteria: The chat resumes without duplicate/missing turns; native session load is used when claimed, otherwise portable replay is explicit.
rubric.evidence: Pre/post state, vendor session id/load trace, transcript diff, and fact probe.

rubric.criterion: Portable history is canonical across providers, preserves complete conversational turns, and excludes internal tool/thought rows from impersonating user or assistant speech.
rubric.passCriteria: Opening decisions and recent complete turns survive; brain stamps are retained; truncation and checkpoint boundaries are disclosed.
rubric.evidence: Serialized portable history, source transcript, and receiving-provider prompt.

rubric.criterion: Fork and rewind preserve explicit parent/child lineage and never mutate the source chat unexpectedly.
rubric.passCriteria: Divergent turns stay isolated, lineage is navigable, and native versus Workhorse ownership is visible.
rubric.evidence: Parent/child ids, transcript comparison, lineage UI, and vendor operation trace.

rubric.criterion: Compaction preserves declared keep-notes and restores enough context to continue without falsely claiming full native memory.
rubric.passCriteria: Post-compact probe recovers the keep-note and key decisions; checkpoint/native source is identifiable.
rubric.evidence: Compact event/checkpoint, context counters, and post-compact answers.

rubric.criterion: Queued prompts, cancellation, and retry cannot append stale output to the wrong chat, branch, provider, or model.
rubric.passCriteria: Canceled output remains canceled, queued work executes once in order, and every result retains its original chat/provider/model identity.
rubric.evidence: Event timeline, queue record, cancel acknowledgement, transcript, and usage rows.

rubric.criterion: Copy/export/support surfaces produce the visible conversation intended by the user without leaking hidden context or secrets.
rubric.passCriteria: Latest-reply copy is exact, export marks provider/model transitions, and hidden prompts/tool credentials are absent.
rubric.evidence: Clipboard/export artifact and secret/hidden-context scan.

areas.title: Usage, plans, budgets, Watch, and support truthfulness

scenarios.name: Reconcile turn usage by provider and actual model
steps: Record the empty baseline, then send one deterministic prompt per profile.
Capture raw provider/API usage events and the finalized Workhorse usage row.
Switch models once and send again.
Reconcile provider totals, model totals, input/output/cache tokens, context, and cost without double counting.

scenarios.name: Inspect plan remaining, budgets, and Watch holds
steps: Load each available vendor plan/remains source and capture timestamp/source.
Set a small fixture budget or deterministic Watch threshold.
Trigger a hold without spending live money and verify the reason plus override scope.
Restart and verify durable marks/permits behave as documented.

scenarios.name: Export a support-safe provider report
steps: Seed canary prompt text, URL, key, environment value, and file content.
Export diagnostics/support information.
Verify build, OS, detections, capabilities, and safe counts are present.
Scan for every canary and confirm none are present.

rubric.criterion: Usage is reachable inside Settings and attributes every real turn to its actual provider and model.
rubric.passCriteria: Provider/model rows match the provenance chain and no preview, failed preflight, or canceled-before-send turn invents tokens.
rubric.evidence: Raw events, finalized usage rows, and Usage UI.

rubric.criterion: Multiple partial/cumulative usage events are deduplicated and finalized without inflation.
rubric.passCriteria: Known cumulative fixtures and live event sequences reconcile exactly once across input/output/cache/cost.
rubric.evidence: Event sequence, deduplication trace, final totals, and independent arithmetic.

rubric.criterion: Context-window and remaining-plan displays state their source and do not confuse context occupancy, subscription remaining, or local budget.
rubric.passCriteria: Each number has provider/model, unit, time/source, and unknown/unlimited behavior; stale data is visibly stale.
rubric.evidence: Plan payload, model context source, Usage/Watch UI, and timestamps.

rubric.criterion: Usage persists and aggregates by Today/Week/Month/All without changing history when models are renamed or catalogs update.
rubric.passCriteria: Historical rows retain stable provider/model keys and range totals equal their underlying events after restart.
rubric.evidence: Usage state before/after restart, range totals, and model catalog change probe.

rubric.criterion: Watch holds are deterministic, explain the exact threshold, persist safely, and never merge budgets across vendors.
rubric.passCriteria: A hold blocks only the intended vendor/session/threshold; permit and day-mark expiry are correct across restart.
rubric.evidence: Watch inputs, hold result, permit record, provider send outcome, and restart state.

rubric.criterion: Support export is useful for adapter diagnosis but excludes prompts, messages, URLs, file contents, environment values, and credentials.
rubric.passCriteria: Safe build/detection/capability metadata exists and every seeded canary is absent.
rubric.evidence: Support report plus automated canary scan.

areas.title: Install, update, persistence, recovery, and release evidence

scenarios.name: Compare source, packaged build, and existing install
steps: Record repository commit, package version, build platform, and installed app version before launch.
Build or obtain the approved package without overwriting the existing install.
Inspect packaged contents for renderer, Electron main, icons, and required resources.
Launch with isolated state and verify the UI can identify its version/build channel.

scenarios.name: Recover state and active work after process interruption
steps: Create projects, chats, an active goal, a scheduled run, and one pending/failed attention item.
Interrupt the app during safe fixture work, then relaunch.
Verify atomic state recovery, backup fallback, queue/goal/schedule recovery, and no duplicate dispatch.
Corrupt only a copied fixture state file and verify backup recovery without touching real user data.

scenarios.name: Exercise update checks, diagnostics, and release gates
steps: Run a mocked current/newer/malformed update check and inspect user-facing results.
Verify the release artifact contains expected files and launches on its claimed platform.
Run the free structural/unit/build verification lane.
Record dependency audit findings separately from product verdicts and do not auto-fix breaking updates.

rubric.criterion: The evaluated build is traceable to an exact source commit, package version, platform, and install channel.
rubric.passCriteria: Source, package, and running app identities are recorded; mismatches stop or invalidate the run rather than being hand-waved.
rubric.evidence: Git commit, package metadata, artifact hash, platform, and in-app version.

rubric.criterion: Install, update, quit, and relaunch preserve user projects/chats while keeping an isolated eval run from overwriting the user's normal state.
rubric.passCriteria: Eval uses isolated userData; update/uninstall policy is explicit; relaunch retains intended state and no real state is mutated.
rubric.evidence: User-data paths, before/after hashes, install/update transcript, and relaunch screenshot.

rubric.criterion: Atomic persistence, backup rotation, migration, and corrupt-primary fallback recover the newest compatible state.
rubric.passCriteria: Fixture corruption recovers from backup with a visible/support-safe diagnostic and without accepting plaintext credentials.
rubric.evidence: State files/hashes, recovery choice, migrated version, and credential scan.

rubric.criterion: Goals, scheduled work, active dispatch, queues, and attention state recover once after restart.
rubric.passCriteria: Each durable item returns with correct status; in-flight work is recovered or failed explicitly; no duplicate provider send occurs.
rubric.evidence: Journal/state before interruption, recovery log, provider send ids, and final attention inbox.

rubric.criterion: Packaged artifacts contain the real renderer/main/resources and update checks fail safely on unavailable or malformed release metadata.
rubric.passCriteria: Artifact inventory meets declared contents and mocked update failures do not corrupt or strand the app.
rubric.evidence: Artifact inventory, launch result, update fixture responses, and UI messages.

rubric.criterion: The free release gate validates eval coverage, TypeScript/build, unit/contract tests, and records dependency risk before any live provider spend.
rubric.passCriteria: npm run verify passes; eval drift fails the gate; dependency audit findings are captured without an automatic breaking fix.
rubric.evidence: Exact command outputs, test counts, build artifact inventory, and dependency-audit summary.
